about.heading: About Lucky Lion eBike
about.body: Lucky Lion eBike is a Cavite-based electric vehicle retailer offering a wide lineup of e-bikes, e-trikes, and e-cars for everyday Filipino riders. From its main branch on Emilio Aguinaldo Highway, Palico II, Imus City, Cavite, Lucky Lion has grown to multiple branches across Cavite and Laguna — including the Trece Martires branch in Brgy. San Agustin. Every unit is backed by lifetime service, flexible payment options (cash, Home Credit installment, and credit card), and free delivery within Cavite and selected areas — Quality Ride, Trusted Performance. In December 2022, Lucky Lion was honored as the Best E-Bike Marketing Company by The World Class Philippines Awards Council.

maintenance.heading: General Maintenance
maintenance.intro: Simple, regular care keeps any Lucky Lion e-bike, e-trike, or e-car safe and long-lasting. These general guidelines apply to all units.
maintenance.source: Maintenance information provided by the Lucky Lion main shop.

items: Brakes firm, tires inflated, and lights / horn / signals working.
Mirrors and seat secure; bolts tight.
Battery charged and locked securely in place.
Wear a helmet appropriate to your unit's class (see Road Rules).
Won't turn on: check the battery charge, main switch, and battery connector.
Reduced range: check tire pressure, avoid overloading; the battery may need servicing.
Brakes rubbing or weak: they need adjustment — visit the branch.
Charger light behaving oddly: let the battery cool, reseat the charger; if it persists, have it checked.
For anything electrical or persistent, contact Lucky Lion Trece — units include lifetime service.
Recharge after every use — don't let a lead-acid battery sit fully drained.
Use only the original charger; unplug once fully charged (about 6–8 hours).
Let the unit cool ~30 minutes after riding before charging; charge in a cool, dry, ventilated place.
If unused for a while, recharge at least once a month to prevent battery damage.
Keep battery terminals clean and dry — never expose the battery to rain or water.
Test the brakes before every ride — they should feel firm and stop smoothly.
Have disc/drum brakes adjusted if they feel loose, weak, or noisy.
Check tire pressure weekly and keep it at the recommended level for safety and range.
Inspect tires for cuts, wear, or embedded objects; replace when the tread is low.
Make sure wheel nuts and axles are tight.
Listen for unusual motor noises — have it checked if it grinds or hesitates.
Keep wiring and connectors dry; avoid deep water and flooded roads.
Don't overload beyond the rated capacity — it strains the motor and controller.
If the unit loses power or cuts out, stop and have the controller and connections inspected.
Wipe with a damp cloth — never pressure-wash or hose down the electricals or battery.
Dry the unit thoroughly after cleaning or riding in the rain.
Store in a covered, dry place away from direct sun and rain.
For long storage, keep the battery around half-to-full charge and top it up monthly.

roadRules._source: Summarized from LTO classification of e-bikes / light electric vehicles (ltoportal.ph, LTO AO 2021-039 / MC VDM-2024). items: Recharge after every use — don't let a lead-acid battery sit empty; deep discharge shortens its life.
Charge fully (about 6–8 hours) and unplug once full to avoid overcharging.
Charge and store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated place — away from direct heat.
If the e-bike is idle, top up the charge at least once a month to prevent sulfation.
Smooth acceleration and steady, moderate speeds stretch your range per charge.
Keep tires at the correct pressure and avoid overloading to get the most range.
Always wear the correct helmet for your unit's class (bicycle or motorcycle helmet).
Do a quick pre-ride check: brakes, tires, lights, horn.
Signal your turns, obey traffic lights, and keep to bike lanes / roads allowed for your class.
Don't exceed the rated passenger/cargo capacity of your unit.
Slow down on wet, gravel, or uneven surfaces; avoid flooded roads to protect the motor and battery.
Keep both hands on the handlebars and avoid using your phone while riding.
Check tire pressure weekly and inspect for wear.
Test and adjust the brakes (disc/drum) regularly for safe stopping.
Re-tighten bolts and fasteners, especially in the first weeks of use.
Clean with a damp cloth — never pressure-wash the electricals or battery box.
Keep lights, horn, and signals working.
Bring your unit in for periodic servicing — Lucky Lion offers lifetime service.
Know your unit's LTO class — it decides whether a helmet, license, or registration is needed (see Road Rules).
Keep your official receipt and warranty papers safe.
Payment options: Cash (with discount), Home Credit installment, or Credit Card.
If your class requires it (L2b, L3, L4/L5, L6/L7), complete LTO registration and licensing.
Follow your local ordinance on where light electric vehicles may be driven.
